title: Smart Sequencer — Batch & Cache Policy Playbook
creator: Sofia Kim
description: Design a compact, decision-focused playbook within the Redwood Console that helps engineers and platform owners create safe, cost-effective batch and cache policies. The playbook should present a sequenced flow: workload characterization -> recommended policy presets -> trade-off explainer -> safety guardrails and rollback steps. Emphasis on short, skimmable microcopy and a simulation sandbox so customers can preview token-cost and latency trade-offs before applying settings.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook UI created as a modular panel in the Console routes page and accessible from model-route configuration
Prototype (Figma) demonstrates sequenced steps with inline explainers and one-click preset application
Simulation sandbox supports at least 3 workload archetypes and shows token-cost and P95 latency delta
Guardrail toggles exposed with clear failure modes and automatic fallback suggestions
Hand-off assets and a 3-slide design summary delivered for handover to ENG and PM
comments: 2026-02-10 Sofia Kim: Initial discovery notes — interviewed 4 internal customers (Platform, Search, Assistant team) about current pain points. Common themes: fear of regressions, unclear cost estimates, and long rollbacks.

2026-02-17 Ava Martínez: Lo-fi flow sketched — propose ‘characterize -> recommend -> simulate -> apply’ linear sequence. Decided to prioritize compact mode for quick apply and expanded mode for operators.

2026-02-20 Design critique: Feedback from PM (Rajesh Patel) — add explicit fallback policy and require non-blocking rollback suggestion when guardrail hit. Also call out required telemetry fields for backend (ENG-3421).
2026-02-24 Prototype v1 uploaded to Figma: https://figma.redwood.example/smart-sequencer/v1 — includes three presets (Conservative, Balanced, Throughput-First) and a cost/latency micro-simulator.

2026-02-26 Engineering sync (ENG owners: Priya Shah) — discussed API surface for applying presets and simulation; backend needs a lightweight simulator endpoint (ENG-3421) and a KV-cache metrics export. Agreed on minimal telemetry contract: p50/p95 latency change, tokens saved estimate, rollback flag.
2026-02-28 Usability test (5 engineers): Observations — users understood presets but wanted clearer definitions of 'prefix cache' vs 'kv-cache', suggested inline examples. Microcopy updates planned.
2026-03-03 PM review (Rajesh Patel): Approved scope for MVP with caveat to avoid modal-driven flows. Request: make the simulation non-destructive and default to dry-run.

2026-03-05 Next steps: polish copy, add guardrail exception rationale panel, prepare Handoff doc and a short demo script for 03/12 engineering handoff meeting. Create ENG ticket for simulator endpoint and telemetry schema (ENG-4120).

Links: PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INF/Smart+Sequencer+Playbook — Prototype: https://figma.redwood.example/smart-sequencer/v1 — Usability notes: https://docs.redwood.example/ux/ss-playbook-usability-02-26
ux_notes: Use progressive disclosure: hide advanced knobs under an 'Advanced' accordion to reduce cognitive load for PLG users.
Microcopy should define technical terms in plain language and include inline 'why this matters' tooltips.
Simulation results should show both absolute and relative (delta) metrics, and a small sparkline for trend context.
Default preset should be 'Balanced' with a one-click revert to previous route config.
Design for keyboard-first flows and accessible color contrast for warning states in guardrails.
Expose an inline link to the rollout plan (canary percentage, duration) when user applies a new policy so they can create a safe rollout in a single flow.
